Stage 1 — read, repair, scope, and collapse to identities

Source: R/pipeline.R, R/prepare.R
pf_prepare.Rd

Wraps pf_read_grants() (which itself calls pf_prepare_grants(), and so pf_standardize_status()), then pf_recover_name_from_street(), pf_dedup(), and pf_recipients().

Turns the raw GTDC 990-PF "grants paid during year" extract (Part XIV Table 3a) into a frame npmatch can consume, and attaches the scope decision.

Usage

pf_prepare(
  grants,
  pattern = "grants.*[.]csv$",
  dedup = c("fuzzy", "exact", "none"),
  threshold = 0.92,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

grants

A directory of grant CSVs, a vector of file paths, or an already-read data frame.

pattern

Regex selecting files when grants is a directory.

dedup

"fuzzy" (default), "exact", or "none".

threshold

Name-similarity threshold for fuzzy clustering.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A list of class pf_prepared with grants (every row, scoped and assigned a recipient_uid), recipients (one row per identity, in scope), and timing.

Details

The dedup step is the scale lever, not a nicety: grants repeat heavily, and matching distinct recipient identities rather than grant rows removes most of the work without removing recall. It also adds recall, because a match found for any cluster member propagates to all of them.

Name fields

The extract carries three recipient-name columns, and the data dictionary is explicit about what they are:

  • SIGOCPYRPNAM — "Name of Grantee — Person"

  • SIGOCPYRBNBN1 — "Name of Grantee — Business Line 1"

  • SIGOCPYRBNBN2 — "Name of Grantee — Business Line 2"

So BNBN1 / BNBN2 are a two-line wrap of one name, not a main name and a DBA — line 2 exists because line 1 ran out of characters. In the 5,000-row sample PNAM and BNBN1 never co-occur (0 rows carry both), so the recipient name is a straight coalesce of the two. PNAM is not a reliable individual flag: filers routinely put organizations in it ("World Central Kitchen", "Surfrider Foundation"), so scope is decided from SIGOCPYRFSTA instead.

Line 2, when present, is one of four things, and each is handled differently:

  1. a duplicate of line 1 — dropped

  2. a care-of / attention line ("ATTN LEGAL DEPARTMENT", "C/O JUDY AREANO") — dropped, it is address data in a name field

  3. an FBO beneficiary ("ROCKY MOUNTAIN COLLEGE FBO" + "ALYSSA PATTERSON") — dropped and the trailing FBO stripped from line 1, since the grantee of record is the college

  4. a genuine continuation ("MEMPHIS JEWISH HOME B'NAI B'RITH HOME &" + "HOSPITAL") — joined onto line 1 as an alternate name

The joined continuation is carried in npmatch's dba slot. That is a deliberate reuse rather than a claim that it is a DBA: np_compare() scores the full name/DBA cross-product and keeps the best, so putting the untruncated name there lets a record match on either the truncated line-1 form or the complete one, whichever the BMF happens to hold.
